Dot Score Rules

Dishwasher exposure score · 8 October 2026

Dot score: Original, D and New, with the G and J jet cones

A dot's score says how exposed it is to the lower spray arm. The original rule (revision 5) can rank a dot that sees one spray point above a dot that sees all 64. Two fixes are compared here. D divides by all 64 lines. New divides by the best-facing dot at the same spot. D and New each come with G or J, which count only near-vertical jets. Sliders show all seven rules for one unblocked dot, computed live, and for the HOTEC plate and bowl, read from a grid of poses, at tilts from 0° (facing the arm) to 180° (facing away).

The rules

One numerator, three denominators

Each dot sends lines to the spray arm's disc (radius R = 23.3 cm). Every rule adds up the same thing on top: the cosine of each open line against the dot's normal. The rules differ only in what they divide by.

d_k unit direction from the dot to the end of line k c_k = max(0, n·d_k) cosine between line k and the dot's normal n; 0 from behind v_k = 1 if line k is open, 0 if something blocks it W(m) = Σ_k max(0, m·d_k) the weight this spot would give a dot whose normal were m Original = Σ_k c_k v_k / W(n) ÷ the dot's own weight D = Σ_k c_k v_k / 64 ÷ the number of lines New = Σ_k c_k v_k / max_m W(m) ÷ the best-facing dot at the same spot D+G, D+J = D's formula over the G or J lines, still ÷ 64 New+G, New+J = New's formula over the G or J lines: both sums run over the same smaller set lines k Original, D, New: the 64 fixed spray points on the disc G: those of the 64 within θ of vertical below the dot J: the dot's own 64 points inside its θ-circle (radius h·tan θ), those that land on the disc empty a dot with no line, or W = 0, scores 0
OriginalOf the spray that could reach me, how much is unblocked? It divides by the dot's own weight, so it cannot see how little could reach. A dot facing one spray point and keeping it scores 1. DHow much spray reaches me, per spray point? This is an absolute amount. Even a perfect dot cannot reach 1, because far spray points arrive at a slant. Its ceiling depends on height: 0.23 at 3 cm, 0.68 at 14 cm, 0.85 at 26 cm. D+GD, counting only the fixed spray points within θ of vertical below the dot. At 14 cm and θ 30° that keeps about 8 of the 64, so even a perfect dot scores about 0.12: the ceiling falls with θ. D+JD over the dot's own 64 near-vertical lines, still ÷ 64. Where the cone lies on the disc its ceiling is 0.928 at 30°, so D+J is New+J × 0.928 there; the two differ only near the disc edge. NewHow much reaches me, as a share of the most that could reach this spot? The reference is the same spot with the normal turned to face the arm as well as possible, with nothing in the way. A dot that faces the best way and is unblocked scores 1 at any height or position. New+GNew, counting only the fixed spray points within θ of vertical below the dot. At 14 cm and θ 30° that keeps about 8 of the 64. New+JNew, counting only near-vertical jets: 64 lines of the dot's own, spread inside its θ-circle. Where the circle lies on the disc, the best-facing dot faces straight down and the reference is a constant (64 × 0.928 at 30°).
14 cm over the disc centre, θ 30°OriginalDNew
Case 1: one spray point straight ahead, kept; the other 63 behind10.0160.023
Case 2: facing the arm, all 64 in front, half of the weight blocked0.50.340.5
Ideal: facing the arm, nothing blocked10.681

The original puts case 1 above case 2. D and New put them in the right order, but only New keeps the ideal dot at 1. The maximum over m is pure geometry: it needs no extra ray cast. It is found by turning m toward the mean direction of the lines it faces, repeated from about 70 starting directions per dot. One start is not enough: on the plate on edge, the search started from the mean of all lines alone settled on a worse direction.

The dot is unblocked and computed live. The plate and the bowl are read from the grid: tilt in 5° steps from 0° to 180°, nine heights, distance in 5 cm steps, ten jet angles. Past 90° the food side turns away from the arm: at 180° the plate lies face up and the bowl mouth up. θ moves only the four cone rules.

Per dot

The plate and the bowl, dot by dot

Goal loads

Shuffled first-fit loads: mostly plates in the front bank

566 random full loads of all 24 HOTEC dishes (8 plates, 8 bowls, 8 cups) were packed by the top-5 run's first-fit packer. Each try shuffles every kind's list of poses, but the order of kinds comes from three presets that put plates first, and 552 of the 566 loads used the one that puts all 8 plates in the front bank. So this is not fully random: see the next section for that. There are no keeps, no ascent and no bans. The only rules were the physical ones from the top-5 run: no appliance or rack-retraction collision, and dishes may touch by up to 0.8 mm. Nested bowls are allowed but scored. Each load was scored under all four rules with the revision-5 dots and blockers. Below are the five highest and five lowest under New, then under New+J. Every panel shows the lower rack from the top, the upper rack from the top, and a side view, and gives S under all four rules.

Goal loads, truly random

Random dish order, random free pose for every dish

This run puts all 24 dishes in one shuffled order with the kinds mixed, and gives each dish a uniformly random free pose from its kind's candidate list. There are no presets, no front-bank rule and no search. The physical rules stay the same: no appliance or rack-retraction collision, and dishes may touch by up to 0.8 mm. A load where any dish finds no free pose is thrown away. Twelve processes sampled for about 12 minutes.

Findings

What the comparison shows

New fixes the edge case and keeps the best pose near the top

Plate on edge: 0.801 under the original, 0.339 under New. Plate facing the arm: 0.998 and 0.938. D also orders the two cases correctly, but its ceiling moves with height: the same plate facing the arm scores 0.26 at 3 cm and 0.79 at 26 cm.

Past 90° every rule falls to 0, the original last

Plate 14 cm up, centred, θ 30°. At 110°, 20° past on edge, the original still gives 0.64; New gives 0.16 and New+J 0.01. At 135° they are 0.09, 0.014 and 0.001. The tilt at which each rule drops to half its facing-the-arm value: original 120°, New 80°, D 75°, New+J 65°, New+G 60°. Face up at 180°, everything is 0 but the original's 0.002 from one or two rim dots. The bowl behaves the same, from lower values.

New+J is flat in height; New peaks in the middle

Plate facing the arm, centred, θ 30°, from 3 to 26 cm: New+J 0.814 to 0.819 and the bowl 0.504 throughout. New goes 0.50, 0.78, 0.92, 0.94, 0.93, 0.91. Low dots score lower under New because, close to the disc, the best-facing direction is sideways rather than straight down, so a dish facing straight down falls short of it. The original climbs from 0.66 to 1.00.

Off-centre, New fades early and New+J fades only past the disc edge

Plate facing the arm, 14 cm up, moved out 0, 10, 20, 30, 35 cm: New 0.94, 0.84, 0.64, 0.46, 0.39; New+J 0.81, 0.83, 0.82, 0.37, 0.16; the original 1.00 to 0.87. Under New, a dish that faces straight down while off-centre is penalised for not tilting toward the disc. Under New+J, it is penalised only once its jets start to miss the disc (edge at 23.3 cm).

D+J is New+J times a constant until the cone leaves the disc; D+G's ceiling moves with θ and height

Centred plate, θ 30°, any height from 3 to 26 cm: D+J = 0.756 = 0.928 × New+J, because the whole cone lands on the disc and the best-facing weight is a constant. Moved out 20 cm, D+J is 0.46 while New+J holds 0.82: D+J loses the lines that miss the disc, New+J divides by the lines that remain. D+G depends on how many fixed points the cone happens to catch: 0.002 at θ 5°, 0.094 at 30°, 0.679 at 85° (then it equals D), and at θ 30° from 0.005 at 3 cm to 0.318 at 26 cm, where New+G holds 0.81 from 8 cm up.

With the best-facing reference, G and J are the same rule except at the extremes

At θ 30° to 60° New+G and New+J agree within 0.01 for both dishes. They part only at θ 5°, where G keeps almost no fixed point (plate 0.13 against 0.81), and at θ 85°, where G keeps all 64 and equals New (0.94 against 0.76). The New+G search now runs the full start set at θ ≥ 60°: the ten poses whose fast search had overstated a dot (worst 1.20 at plate 3 cm, θ 80°) are recomputed, and no dot exceeds 1 in any rule over the 40,640 dish poses.

Revision 5 (the original) is still the live scorer; exposure.py is unchanged and nothing is committed.
